answer: The cipher multiplier is published, charged in inlet, and tide lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1208 identities would post 3890 proofs and burn roughly 79 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
